title: University of Michigan consumer sentiment — preliminary (Nov 2026), the last reading whose interviews close before the polls open
source: UMICH: TWO of the publisher's own 2026 scheduling documents, both re-fetched direct and PDF-inflated 2026-10-07 by this event's own initial research (same byte counts the proposing lane recorded 2026-09-10). (1) `2026 Release Dates`, data.sca.isr.umich.edu/fetchdoc.php?docid=79628 (HTTP 200, 132,710 bytes), whose text layer reads verbatim "November 6 / November Prelim" alongside all twelve months. (2) `2026 Interview Dates`, fetchdoc.php?docid=79629 (HTTP 200, 89,846 bytes), whose November row reads verbatim "October 20 IW Begins / November 2 Prelim Ends / November 16 IW Ends". Promoted estimate -> confirmed and EST: -> UMICH: on the umich-sentiment-final-2026-09-25 and umich-sentiment-final-2026-11-20 precedents (each promoted off the same publisher documents in its own initial research). NO CLOCK TIME appears in either document and the apex host sca.isr.umich.edu still does not resolve (curl exit 000 on 2026-10-07), so 10:00 ET is CUSTOMARY, NOT SOURCED; confirmed is a claim about the scheduled date only. Originally proposed 2026-09-10 as proposals/umich-sentiment-prelim-2026-11-06.from-umich-sentiment-final-2026-11-20.json, whose finding this canonical file carries forward
notes: Interviews run 2026-10-20 -> 11-02 (published, docid=79629): they END MONDAY 11-02, one day before midterm-elections-2026-11-03 opens the polls, so this is the last national consumer read taken entirely pre-election, and the window CONTAINS fomc-2026-10-28, pce-2026-10-29, gdp-q3-2026-advance-2026-10-29 and eci-q3-2026-10-30 but no CPI (Sept CPI prints 10-14, before the window; Oct CPI 11-10, after it). The release lands two hours after jobs-2026-11-06 (08:30 ET), so its 10:00 ET tape cannot be attributed to the survey. Impact kept `medium` to match umich-sentiment-prelim-2026-09-11: 2026's eight prelims missed consensus by a median |1.75| points, so the surprise gap is structurally live on prelims even though the print is not tradeable (`symbols: []`, no macro-keyed house playbook). The tier remains a judgment for the owning lane's later pulses to revisit. Read-it-do-not-trade-it.
